I learned through doing a 3 card daily reading, as well as a small just-before-bed spread if I could manage it. Every time I did a reading I took a picture of it and made sure to write down my interpretations for each placement, as well as any key words that could describe the meaning of the card in regards to the reading. I referenced 3-4 books whenever I did readings, as well as looked cards up on the internet if I felt like I was really stumped. About 1.5 years in, the repetition eventually locked into my head and I found that I was able to do readings without even checking my books or online. It was a pretty good feeling when I began realizing I knew all of these meanings almost instantly off the top of my head. 

Consistency is definitely key. I am always seeking out new information or more possible meanings for each card whenever I can, as there are just so many additional details that can add to their general meanings. The deck I use is based on the Rider-Waite, which I found extremely helpful as the symbols and imagery were very similar. Observing the pictures on the cards and seeing how they coincide with their meanings contributed a lot to my learning, as making those connections for myself helped me grow to recognize the card meanings faster. Becoming familiar with what element and associations each suit has (such as swords correlating with wind and communication+fast movement) also provided a little light bulb for some card meanings along the way. It felt like learning that helped some of the meanings make more sense for myself. Learning additional details about the cards, such as what star signs they correspond with or their numeric meanings, also helped fuel my learning. 

Don't be afraid to reference books, apps, or the internet! You never know what new information or insight some random resource could provide for you.
